chunk_text: Salamence can break balanced teams by forcing opponents to respect both physical and special attacks. Draco Meteor pressures physical walls, while a physical follow-up punishes special walls that try to absorb it. Entry hazards make these switches increasingly expensive. Its weaknesses and recoil mean it should enter through a slow pivot, a double switch, or after a teammate faints rather than absorbing repeated attacks.
title: Salamence as a mixed wallbreaker

chunk_text: Salamence appreciates teammates that set entry hazards and pressure bulky Steel types. Stealth Rock and Spikes turn its forced switches into lasting progress, while Magnezone can remove some Steel-type answers. Rapid Spin support helps preserve Salamence because its Flying typing leaves it vulnerable to Stealth Rock. The team still needs a plan for faster revenge killers after Salamence has taken recoil or hazard damage.
title: Support for Salamence

chunk_text: Choice Band Scizor compresses revenge killing, scouting, and trapping into one slot. Bullet Punch gives the team priority against weakened offensive threats, U-turn preserves momentum when the opponent switches, and Pursuit can punish vulnerable Psychic- and Ghost-type targets. Being locked into one move creates free turns for resistant setup sweepers, so the user should identify the opponent's likely response before choosing an attack.
title: Choice Band Scizor role

chunk_text: Rotom-Wash fits defensive teams by checking several physical attackers while discouraging Rapid Spin. Its Electric and Ghost pressure can force switches, and Will-O-Wisp reduces the threat posed by physical attackers that lack a safe status absorber. It should not be treated as permanent recovery-based walling: repeated attacks, sand, and entry hazards wear it down, so preserve its health for the specific threats it must check.
title: Defensive Rotom-Wash role

chunk_text: Tyranitar starts sand and can convert forced switches into progress through Stealth Rock, strong attacks, or Pursuit pressure. Sand supports teams built to accumulate residual damage, but it also wears down allies that lack immunity or reliable recovery. Building around Tyranitar therefore means checking whether each teammate benefits from the weather, tolerates it, or becomes easier for the opponent to exhaust.
title: Building around Tyranitar sand

chunk_text: Skarmory uses its defensive profile to place Spikes against physical attackers that cannot threaten it immediately. Whirlwind compounds hazard damage and prevents many setup attempts from becoming wins. Magnezone and strong special attackers can exploit or remove it, so Skarmory should be paired with teammates that punish those answers rather than being expected to cover every physical threat by itself.
title: Skarmory hazard-setting role

chunk_text: Great Tusk often compresses entry-hazard control, physical bulk, and offensive pressure into one team slot. Rapid Spin removes hazards while improving its ability to pressure slower teams, and it can set Stealth Rock when the team needs its own hazard setter. Because it lacks reliable recovery, repeated switching and status can prevent it from performing every assigned job throughout a long game.
title: Great Tusk role compression

chunk_text: When Great Tusk is the team's only hazard remover, preserve enough health to enter after hazards are established. Trading it early for damage may leave grounded teammates exposed for the rest of the battle. Knock Off support and pressure against Ghost-type switch-ins make Rapid Spin easier to use. If the team already has alternative removal, Great Tusk can play more aggressively and trade health for progress.
title: Preserving Great Tusk for hazard control

chunk_text: Gholdengo supports hazard-stacking teams by making common removal attempts difficult and threatening passive turns with strong attacks or setup. It works best when teammates can repeatedly establish Stealth Rock or Spikes and force the opponent to attempt removal. Gholdengo is not a substitute for every defensive answer, and careless switching can leave it too weakened to contest hazard control later.
title: Gholdengo on hazard-stacking teams

chunk_text: Dragapult gives offensive teams immediate speed control and can maintain momentum with pivoting moves. Its flexible physical, special, and status options make the first response difficult to choose, but each set gives up coverage or utility found on another set. Identify whether the team needs direct damage, disruption, or scouting before selecting the moveset rather than treating Dragapult's flexibility as access to every option at once.
title: Dragapult as speed control

chunk_text: Kingambit is most dangerous when opposing checks have been weakened and its team has created an endgame where priority can control faster threats. Revealing it too early can let the opponent preserve dedicated answers or exploit its reliance on prediction. The rest of the team should make progress against bulky Fighting-, Ground-, and Fire-type responses so Kingambit is not asked to break every answer and clean in the same sequence.
title: Preparing a Kingambit endgame

chunk_text: Counterplay to Kingambit should combine a healthy defensive answer with positioning that denies a free setup turn. Relying only on a faster attacker is risky because priority can bypass normal speed control. Keep the intended answer outside the range of its attacks, avoid sacrificing pieces that strengthen its endgame, and pressure it before the rest of the team has been reduced to targets it can finish with priority.
title: Planning counterplay to Kingambit
